subject: Soft eviction grace request for long-running training jobs
messages:
From: Michael Cole <michael.cole@orbishealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: grace window for long-running training during maintenance

Hi Marcus,

Quick ask from our infra team at Orbis — we run nightly training jobs for our clinical QA model that typically run ~8-12 hours (single job). We have a scheduled Redwood maintenance window next month (Oct 14-16) and those jobs are at high risk of being evicted mid-run. Eviction means requeueing the job and a 10-12 hour delay, which breaks our SLA for nightly updates.

Can Redwood offer a "soft eviction" grace for those long-running jobs within our Dedicated pool (or schedule a temporary reservation) so the jobs can finish before eviction? Ideally: a 12-hour eviction grace window or a reserved slice for those nights. This would be temporary — we're proposing two weeks of trial + engineering changes on our side to shorten runs long-term.

Details attached: sample run profile and our maintenance calendar. Happy to jump on a quick call.

--
Michael Cole
Head of Platform Ops, Orbis Health
O: 415-555-0111
Attachment: maintenance_calendar_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Michael Cole <michael.cole@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: grace window for long-running training during maintenance

Thanks Michael — looping in Product Ops (Kimberly), Infra (Dev) and our pool steward (Laura) to assess options.

Quick asks to help scope the request:
- Are these nightly runs fixed to a single start time (e.g., 10PM PST) or do they vary?
- Is there flexibility to run a lower-throughput version if eviction occurs (smaller batch size / quantized model)?
- Can you share historical eviction/logs for the last 30 days?

I attached a short CSV with the run profile you sent — helps us estimate reservation sizing.

Proposed next steps: Dev to advise on feasibility of a temporary autoscale exception vs. a scheduled reservation; Laura to provide ops impact estimate; Kimberly to sign off on an exception policy if needed.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: prov-training-profile.csv (csv)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Michael Cole <michael.cole@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: grace window for long-running training during maintenance

Appreciate the context. A couple of operational notes from capacity planning:

- We can provision a temporary reservation (1-2 GPU slices) for the requested maintenance nights, but it has tradeoffs: it reduces available burst capacity for other enterprise pilots.
- Alternative: implement an "eviction grace" setting for jobs tagged with a training quota label — infra would honor in-priority termination windows for up to 12 hours if capacity allows. This is more complex but doesn't permanently carve capacity.

My recommendation: start with a 2-week trial using a scheduled reservation for the nights of Oct 14-28 (reserve 1 GPU slice during 00:00-12:00 PST) while Orbis implements shorter runs or checkpointing. If infra flags high contention, we'll pivot to a grace-policy with strict TTL.

I'll attach a short ops estimate for the reserved slice impact. Dev — can you run a quick simulation on the week-of-Oct-14 to validate?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: reserve-ops-estimate.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Michael Cole <michael.cole@orbishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: grace window for long-running training during maintenance

+1 to Laura's runbook. A few technical items to call out:

- Autoscale exceptions are doable but introduce fairness edge cases (we'd need temporary quota tickets and a timeboxed exception).
- If we implement a short-term reservation, we should attach an automated policy that revokes after X windows (suggest 6 weeks) to avoid drift.
- We can also add a maintenance-aware scheduler hook: jobs that detect an upcoming maintenance window will checkpoint and use a cached KV prefix to reduce rework. That reduces the need for reservations long-term.

I've opened a runbook ticket for the simulation and ops automation: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1259 — please add any test payloads. I'll attach the runbook draft.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ops-runbook.md (md)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Cole <michael.cole@orbishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Action plan proposal: Orbis maintenance window (Oct 14-28 trial)

Summary and proposed mutual action plan (MAA):

1) Scope: Orbis Health — nightly long-run training jobs (sample attached).
2) Trial period: Oct 14 - Oct 28 (inclusive) — Reserve 1 GPU slice from 00:00-12:00 PST for Orbis in the us-dedicated pool.
3) Safeguards:
   - Reservation limited to max 2 concurrent slices across Orbis account.
   - Auto-revoke after 6 weeks unless Product Ops approves extension.
   - If pool contention >75% for baseline traffic, infra to trigger fallback and notify Orbis.
4) Deliverables:
   - Dev: run a simulation by Oct 7 and post results to INFRA-1259.
   - Laura: ops impact estimate posted by EOD Sep 29.
   - Orbis: provide 30 days of eviction logs and commit to implementing checkpointing within the 2-week trial.

Kimberly — requesting approval to proceed under these conditions. If approved I will confirm dates with Orbis and schedule the reservation ticket.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Cole <michael.cole@orbishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Action plan proposal: Orbis maintenance window (Oct 14-28 trial)

Approved with conditions:

- Approve the 2-week reservation (Oct 14-28) for 1 GPU slice, limited to US region only.
- Cap: 2 slices max across Orbis during the trial.
- Auto-revoke: Reservation automatically removed after 6 weeks from start date (no manual renewal).
- Monitoring: Product Ops will add a temporary dashboard to track eviction-rate and pool-utilization; if contention crosses 75% persistently for 12+ hours, infra should kill non-tagged low-priority jobs first.

Please file an SLA-exception record: EXC-2026-198 and add the INFRA ticket link. Marcus — proceed to confirm with Orbis and coordinate scheduling.

Kimberly Park
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
